messages:
maya: quick heads-up — we finished the v1 rollout of Dynamic Latency Shaper across the default serving fleet :tada:
maya: TL;DR: p50 down ~22%, p95 down ~11%, overall token cost ~9% lower on our mid-size conversation workload (avg seq ~512).
maya: full canary run finished at 02:10 UTC, no infra errors, traces look clean for 90% of traffic.
oliver: congrats! link to canary dashboard?
canary-bot: canary 2024-11-15-DSL-v1 completed — success threshold met for latency and error budget. Metrics: p50 -21.7%, p95 -10.9%, p99 +2.8% (see links).
tom: saw the canary summary — nice work. quick note: p99 increased for a small slice of long-context requests (>=8k tokens) on models bertx-32k and lamp-24k. Not widespread but worth calling out.
maya: good catch. DSL v1 intentionally trades off rare very-long-tail p99s to prioritize typical conversational latency. We did two things: tighter microburst smoothing + aggressive prefix coalescing. That explains the hit on very long contexts.
product-cw: is this customer-visible? need a line for release notes / changelog. any impact on SLA?
maya: customer-visible only as improved latency and lower cost for most apps. We'll add a changelog entry: "Dynamic Latency Shaper v1: improved median and tail latency for typical sequences; minor degradation for ultra-long contexts (opt-out available)." No SLA change.
maya: rollout plan: default ON for hosted and dedicated pools, opt-out via route config `latency_shaper: off` or per-model flag `dsl_v1: false`. Example config snippet:
```
route_config:
  model: conv-medium
  latency_shaper:
    enabled: true
    mode: dynamic_v1
```
release-bot: rollout event recorded: rollout/DSL-v1 by maya at 2024-11-15T02:05:23Z (canary -> gradual).
s-reliability: please add a p99 alert for >2.5s on requests >8k tokens, and an automated rollback playbook link. I'll add dashboards.
maya: will do. Also kicking off an A/B test next week to test a softer shaping curve that hopefully recovers the long-context p99 without losing p50 gains.
oliver: can we get a short bench note for finance on the ~9% cost improvement? tag me and I'll forward.
maya: ack — I'll drop the summary and a few numbers in the internal benchmark doc and ping you.
tom: if we start seeing increased 5xxs or GPU OOMs, automatic rollback threshold is 0.5% error delta over baseline — keep an eye.
maya: noted. huge thanks team — big perf win for normal workloads, plan in place for long-context customers. :champagne:
